capture.final_message:
Use the characterization of flat modules as modules whose tensor functor preserves injective linear maps.

For the first conjunct, tensor the injection \(f:R\to M\) with \(N\). Flatness of \(N\) makes
\[
R\otimes_R N \longrightarrow M\otimes_R N
\]
injective. Since \(R\otimes_R N\simeq N\) and \(N\) is nontrivial, the codomain is nontrivial.

For the second, replace the restricted families by the induced injections
\[
R^{(s)}\hookrightarrow M,\qquad R^{(t)}\hookrightarrow N
\]
from the corresponding finitely supported free modules. Factor their tensor map as
\[
R^{(s)}\otimes R^{(t)}
\hookrightarrow M\otimes R^{(t)}
\hookrightarrow M\otimes N.
\]
The first arrow is injective because \(R^{(t)}\) is free, hence flat; the second is injective by the assumed flatness of \(M\). Finally identify
\[
R^{(s)}\otimes R^{(t)}\simeq R^{(s\times t)},
\]
whose standard basis maps to the pure tensors \(v_i\otimes w_j\). Their images are therefore linearly independent on \(s\times t\). The essential asymmetry is that flatness of \(M\) is needed for the second injection, while the other tensor factor is automatically flat because it is free.
